note: Engine: فئة واحدة (16:49) = 'only one?'; زعلتكش عن (32:14) = her عن; إدام (51:19) = qdaam, plural of قديم. Medi's -at past endings (maratat 30:11, تلجات 36:45) are sound shape, not B5. The 40:24 أجو moment is one vocab row; the plural أجو/أجا was his own observation.

row.why: تفتتلي is not a word; he then said in English 'the lesson that you planned'. Amal only asked what he meant and gave no word, so it is let-pass. May also be an engine garble - low.

rulings.why: Real non-word for 'planned' (his own English at 15:13 confirms the meaning); Amal's كيف يعني shows she did not understand but supplied nothing. Separate piece from agreed A12 (اللي).

row.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
row.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
row.right: بتطلع = rises / goes up (not بتتطلع = look at)
row.why: He understood her امتى الشمس بتطلع as 'when do you watch the sky'; she said No and explained بتطلع here = goes up; he then said 'بتطلع, not بتتطلع'.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same listening slip; the misheard word in her line is بتطلع, so that is the wrong piece.

row.medi_said: does it has to do with Azan? ... أنا نسيت الكلمة بس سجر. سجر؟
row.amal_said: أذان؟ No. أذان is the call to prayer. فجر.
row.why: He said he forgot the word for dawn (أنا نسيت الكلمة) and guessed أذان; Amal supplied فجر. His سجر is a one-letter root slip of the word she then gave (S4), so the row is a didn't-know.

rulings.why: One moment, one row: a didn't-know (he said he forgot the word). D10 (سجر) is the same moment and a one-letter root slip.

S4/S5: 'mara-mara-maratat' is a stuttered مطرت with the ط softened (Levantine 3fs past is -at); Amal herself called it a tongue twister and he said هذا tongue twister. Pronunciation, not a wrong word.

row.why: سنان is a different word (teeth - he said so himself); Amal asked 'What's سنان?' and gave سنين. A different lexical item = tier 1, not a wrong form of سنين.

rulings.why: Tier 1: سنان is its own word (teeth), not a form of سنة/سنين he invented.
S4 sound shape: تلجات vs her تَلَّجَت is the missing doubled middle letter and a vowel (F2/F3, not scored); he had already said تلجت at 35:25 and Amal said ممتاز, so the past form itself was right.

row.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟ Tell me it was very strong. The wind was very strong in the mornings.
row.why: 'The wind came a lot' made no sense to Amal: she asked إيش يعني twice and gave 'it was very strong'; he then said الهوا كان قوي كتير. Her fix is about meaning (wrong verb), not the plural ending - he noticed 'it's singular' himself.
row.english: the wind was very strong in the morning

rulings.why: Her voiced reaction is to the meaning (إيش يعني x2, then the English 'it was very strong'), so vocab tier 1. The plural أجو for singular الهوا was his own observation after her echo, not a fix she voiced. D12 is the same row.

row.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
row.why: مفضل is an adjective and takes no possessive ending ('Never takes pronoun ending', 54:56); 'my favorite' alone is المفضل عندي. Filed A7 like agreed A37 (same rule, same lesson).
row.english: the second stone was my favorite

rulings.why: An existing bucket fits (A7 noun + adjective, as agreed A37 files the same rule), so not PROPOSE.

row.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
row.why: He used في as 'is' (his book 'isn't here'); Amal: 'في is not is. في is there is' - Arabic needs no word for 'is', just مش هون. That is C1, not a wrong vocab item.

rulings.why: Amal named the rule (في is not 'is'), which is C1 (no word for to be).
Duplicate of D3 (same moment 18:42-18:50); سجر for فجر is a one-letter root slip (S4) inside a didn't-know - he said أنا نسيت الكلمة.

row.medi_said: الشمس و و يوم شو، شو في.
row.right: غير شمس و يوم شو في
row.why: She asked what is there OTHER than sun and day; he dropped غير and said الشمس with el-. Amal recast غير شمس و يوم, he asked 'غير الشمس?' and she repeated غير شمس (8eir + bare noun).
row.english: what is there other than the sun and the day

rulings.why: Real voiced recast: he asked about the el- and she repeated غير شمس. A16 (8eir + noun).
Duplicate of D7 (same moment 40:24, same piece أجو -> كان قوي).
Not an error: a bare time noun used as an adverb (الصبح / الصباح, 'in the morning') is normal Levantine; Amal said Nice to الهوا كان قوي كتير الصباح and never touched it.

row.why: He offered رمل for dirt/soil; Amal told him it means sand; he then found تراب and she said Great job, تراب is dirt or soil.

rulings.why: Wrong lexical item for 'dirt'; her 'رملة sand' tells him it is the wrong word (same treatment as agreed A21's guessed لا).

Not a slip: إدام؟ was a one-word question checking the plural of 'old' (she answered أها = yes). His sentence was 'the streets are old' where the predicate adjective correctly has no el-; the el- came only when Amal rebuilt it as a phrase (الشوارع الإدام في أمريكا حجر).

challenges.why: Amal accepted بعيد: after 'What's the word?' she only gave the preposition (عن) and said ممتاز to بعيد عن الهوا هناك (32:33-32:42). 'What's the word?' (32:08) may be asking for the preposition, not rejecting بعيد; غير عن (32:47) was his own later rewording. Possibly not a vocab slip.

Amal answered واحدة شمس with 'Mm-hmm. واحدة. Great job.' - she praised it and voiced no fix; his feminine واحدة was what she wanted. Word order (شمس وحدة) is only the reader's reading; may not be an error at all.
